walkthrough: The arrow is a projectile with negligible air resistance, so horizontal velocity $v_x$ is constant and vertical acceleration is $g$ downwards.
Horizontal displacement from the archer is $s_x = v_x t$. This is directly proportional to time, a straight line through the origin.
That linear through-origin shape matches graph $q$, so $q$ could be the horizontal component of displacement.
Vertical displacement from launch is $s_y = u_y t - \frac{1}{2}gt^{2}$. It increases at first, reaches zero vertical velocity at the peak of the path, then decreases.
That rise-then-fall curved shape starting and ending at zero matches graph $r$, so $r$ could be the vertical component of displacement.
Graph $p$ shows a quantity that does not change with time, such as a velocity component, not a displacement that grows. This is option B
